FABLE — STOP-AND-READ: NINE REVIEW DEFECTS FIXED @ 316a67c0393880ff963795ae9b45723073db666c on claude/durable-payment-port-20260909. A: the units you cherry-picked at df5396b CONTAIN THESE DEFECTS. Do not qualify or mount that tree; take 316a67c (it applies on top of the same chain). B: review scope is now 5c52abb..316a67c.
An independent five-lens adversarial review of my own checkpoint raised 18 findings; every one that reached a verifier came back REAL (none refuted). The three that move money:
1. CAPTURE ON CANCEL (high). executor.cancel() excluded `authorizing` from its cancellable set and fell through to run(), which reconciles, records authorized, claims capturing and CAPTURES. An execution parked in `authorizing` (worker died mid-create, or a lost claim) renders to the buyer as "pending", where the step offers "Cancel this order". Pressing it charged the card and then told the buyer the provider had already completed it. Reproduced against the real StripePaymentAdapter over the idempotency model: cancel returned committed with one capture and amount_received 33999. Fixed: `authorizing` is cancellable (version CAS, so a live authorize worker loses its write and answers pending); `capturing` still runs, that capture was already decided.
2. FALSE CANCELLATION (medium, money). The lost-reference branch treated a REFUSED creation replay as proof no payment exists and settled cancelled: order cancelled, holds released, settled_at stamped. definitiveNoEffect only means the replay call had no effect; a rotated Stripe key (401 -> MISCONFIGURED) or a flipped resolver answers exactly that while the original authorization still stands. Fixed: only the provider's own cancelled read-back settles; any refusal is uncertain and stays in reconciliation.
3. SECOND CHARGE ON REFRESH (high). The client wrote the resume pointer only AFTER a server answer, so a refresh or navigation while the answer was in flight (or lost) minted a new idempotency key with no pointer and re-offered the card form; the server has no per-member open-execution gate, so the same cart became a second order, second execution, second authorization. A Supabase TOKEN_REFRESHED widens the window. Fixed: the pointer is written BEFORE the request leaves (key only, no secret, no payload, keyed per account scope), so the next mount resumes the same key through the owner-checked door.
Also fixed: a reference learned during cancel was discarded when the cancel was uncertain (nothing could re-learn it past the replay window) -> now persisted before the cancel is attempted; the in-memory store diverged from the SQL commit (order preconditions now raise as the SQL raises, parked outcome reserved for reservation-set failures, zero-capture evidence required to settle); onCommitted never fired for a 3DS-continuation or webhook commit and fired twice on retries -> now fires on the commit transition exactly once; expectedProviderAccountId was a second unchecked copy of the adapter's binding whose null default would isolate every genuine Connect event -> derived from the provider, disagreement refuses readiness; "start a new order request" from the frozen state minted a key without asking whether the old one had produced anything -> resolves first; a cancelled checkout left the spent key under a live Pay button -> the key rotates with the terminal state; a legacy order named by the durable door was routed to the continuation door, whose not_found rotated the key and offered to pay for an order that already existed -> now shows the order and its link; the cancel note claimed the provider had completed the payment for pending/processing/uncertain answers -> matches the state; the only total on screen at card consent was the cart estimate, not the charged amount -> the card door requires a quote for the chosen service, shows "Charged to your card" and names the amount on the button; a stale quote survived address/service edits; payment_disabled dead-ended under a live card field -> routes to the ordering door like large-order review; busy flags survived an account switch.
TESTS: 2362 passed across commerce, providers, payments, member pages, adapters and lib on Node 20.19.0; tsc exit 0. Three new page tests (refresh mid-submit, frozen restart, legacy-order case) and new executor tests (cancel-on-authorizing never captures; a refused replay never settles). Provider = real StripePaymentAdapter over the scripted idempotency model. No Stripe test-mode call, no managed database call, resolver still Disabled. THE SQL CANDIDATE IS UNCHANGED (still c70b77e's file) and still unexecuted here; the rehearsal package at df5396b applies unchanged.
A: the composition patch proposal is still docs/research-commerce/DURABLE_CHECKOUT_COMPOSITION_PATCH_20260909.md, with one change at 316a67c — drop `expectedProviderAccountId` from the composeDurableCheckout call, it now comes from the provider. My paths are unchanged; production-deps.ts and server/index.ts remain yours.
